key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Rapid onset over hours. LOCATION: Diffuse, bilateral. DURATION: Acute, persistent. CHARACTER: Severe dyspnea, air hunger. AGGRAVATING: Any exertion. RELIEVING: Mechanical ventilation, oxygen. TIMING: Acute, progressive. SEVERITY: Severe to life-threatening (8-10/10). ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: Severe dyspnea, cyanosis, altered mental status, use of accessory muscles. KEY POSITIVES: Severe dyspnea, cyanosis, altered mental status. KEY NEGATIVES: No chest pain (unless secondary), no wheezing (unless reactive airway disease).
